defmodule Dhc.Email.Worker do
  @moduledoc """
  Oban worker that sends transactional emails via the Loops API.

  Migrated from the `process-emails` Deno edge function. Each job represents
  a single email (one Oban job per message, replacing the pgmq batch-read
  pattern).

  ## Job args

    * `email` — the recipient email address
    * `transactional_id` — a friendly template name (`"inviteMember"`,
      `"workshopAnnouncement"`, `"workshopRegistration"`,
      `"workshopRegistrationError"`, `"magicLink"`). The worker translates
      this to the real Loops dashboard transactional ID via the
      `:loops_transactional_ids` app env map (mirroring the edge function's
      env-var lookup).
    * `data_variables` — key-value pairs injected into the email template
      (values must be strings or numbers)

  ## Friendly name → Loops ID translation

  The arg carries a friendly name; Loops wants the dashboard-generated ID
  (e.g. `clfq6dinn000yl70fgwwyp82l`). Translation happens at send time via
  `Application.get_env(:dhc, :loops_transactional_ids)`, a map keyed by
  friendly name. The map is built in `config/runtime.exs` and `config/dev.exs`
  from the `INVITE_MEMBER_TRANSACTIONAL_ID`,
  `WORKSHOP_ANNOUNCEMENT_TRANSACTIONAL_ID`,
  `WORKSHOP_REGISTRATION_TRANSACTIONAL_ID`, and
  `WORKSHOP_REGISTRATION_ERROR_TRANSACTIONAL_ID` env vars.

  Only `workshopRegistration` has a real Loops ID as its fallback default
  (`cmnok76cq02tq0ix92oeoi1kk`). The other three **must** be set in
  production or the worker fails fast with
  `{:error, {:transactional_id_not_configured, friendly_name}}` — it never
  sends the friendly name to Loops (that produces a 404 after 5 retries).

  ## Environment behaviour

    * **dev/test** — delivers the Loops payload (recipient, friendly template
      name, data variables) as plain JSON to the local Mailpit relay via the
      `:email_dev_mailer` module (`Dhc.Email.DevMailer` by default, SMTP to
      `localhost:1025`, web UI `http://localhost:8025`). Delivery failures are
      logged and swallowed — a stopped Mailpit container must never fail or
      retry dev jobs — so the job always succeeds even if the relay is down.
    * **prod** — POSTs to `https://app.loops.so/api/v1/transactional` using
      the `LOOPS_API_KEY` environment variable

  Oban handles retries with exponential backoff. If the Loops API returns
  a non-2xx response, the job returns `{:error, reason}` and will be retried
  up to `max_attempts` times.

  ## Logging

  Every log line carries the Oban job context (`oban_job_id`, `oban_attempt`,
  `oban_queue`, `oban_worker`) plus `email` and `transactional_id`. The Loops
  request/response is logged at debug level (without the API key) so failures
  can be correlated to a specific job and HTTP exchange.
  """

  use Oban.Worker, queue: :emails, max_attempts: 5

  require Logger

  @transactional_ids ~w(inviteMember workshopAnnouncement workshopRegistration workshopRegistrationError magicLink)
  # Default Loops API URL. Overridable via app config for tests.
  defp loops_api_url,
    do: Application.get_env(:dhc, :loops_api_url, "https://app.loops.so/api/v1/transactional")

  @impl Worker
  def perform(%Oban.Job{args: args} = job) do
    ctx = job_log_context(job)

    with :ok <- validate_args(args, ctx),
         :ok <- send_email(args, ctx) do
      :ok
    else
      {:error, reason} = error ->
        Logger.error(
          "[email-worker] Job failed: #{format_reason(reason)}",
          Keyword.merge(ctx,
            email: args["email"],
            transactional_id: args["transactional_id"],
            reason: format_reason(reason)
          )
        )

        error
    end
  end

  defp validate_args(args, ctx) do
    errors =
      []
      |> validate_required(args, "email")
      |> validate_email_format(args)
      |> validate_required(args, "transactional_id")
      |> validate_transactional_id(args)
      |> validate_data_variables(args)

    case errors do
      [] ->
        :ok

      errors ->
        message = "Invalid email job args: #{Enum.join(errors, ", ")}"

        Logger.error(
          "[email-worker] #{message}",
          Keyword.merge(ctx,
            email: args["email"],
            transactional_id: args["transactional_id"],
            validation_errors: Enum.join(errors, ", ")
          )
        )

        Sentry.capture_message(message,
          level: :error,
          extra: %{
            args: args,
            validation_errors: errors,
            oban_job_id: ctx[:oban_job_id],
            oban_attempt: ctx[:oban_attempt],
            oban_queue: ctx[:oban_queue],
            oban_worker: ctx[:oban_worker]
          }
        )

        {:error, {:validation, errors}}
    end
  end

  defp validate_required(errors, args, field) do
    if is_nil(args[field]) or args[field] == "" do
      ["missing #{field}" | errors]
    else
      errors
    end
  end

  defp validate_email_format(errors, %{"email" => email}) when is_binary(email) do
    if email =~ ~r/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/ do
      errors
    else
      ["invalid email format" | errors]
    end
  end

  defp validate_email_format(errors, _args), do: errors

  defp validate_transactional_id(errors, %{"transactional_id" => id})
       when id in @transactional_ids,
       do: errors

  defp validate_transactional_id(errors, _args),
    do: ["invalid transactional_id" | errors]

  defp validate_data_variables(errors, %{"data_variables" => vars}) when is_map(vars) do
    invalid_values =
      Enum.any?(vars, fn
        {_k, v} when is_binary(v) -> false
        {_k, v} when is_number(v) -> false
        _ -> true
      end)

    if invalid_values do
      ["data_variables values must be strings or numbers" | errors]
    else
      errors
    end
  end

  defp validate_data_variables(errors, _args), do: errors

  defp send_email(%{"transactional_id" => transactional_id} = args, ctx) do
    if env() == :prod do
      with {:ok, loops_id} <- resolve_loops_id(transactional_id, ctx) do
        post_to_loops(args, loops_id, ctx)
      end
    else
      deliver_dev_email(args, ctx)
    end
  end

  defp env do
    Application.get_env(:dhc, :environment, :development)
  end

  # Non-prod delivery: the raw Loops payload as JSON through the dev mailer
  # seam (Mailpit by default). The job never fails on delivery errors — the
  # dev relay being down is an expected condition (e.g. the compose service
  # was never started), not something to retry 5 times into Oban's discard.
  defp deliver_dev_email(
         %{"email" => email, "transactional_id" => transactional_id} = args,
         ctx
       ) do
    payload = %{
      email: email,
      transactional_id: transactional_id,
      data_variables: Map.get(args, "data_variables", %{})
    }

    subject = "[dev] Loops email: #{transactional_id}"
    body = Jason.encode!(payload, pretty: true)

    case dev_mailer().deliver(email, subject, body) do
      :ok ->
        Logger.info(
          "[email-worker] Email delivered to Mailpit (dev)",
          Keyword.merge(ctx, email: email, transactional_id: transactional_id)
        )

        :ok

      {:error, reason} ->
        Logger.warning(
          "[email-worker] Mailpit delivery failed (is `docker compose up -d mailpit` running?), job will not retry",
          Keyword.merge(ctx,
            email: email,
            transactional_id: transactional_id,
            reason: inspect(reason)
          )
        )

        :ok
    end
  end

  defp dev_mailer, do: Application.get_env(:dhc, :email_dev_mailer, Dhc.Email.DevMailer)

  defp resolve_loops_id(friendly_name, ctx) do
    # Translation mirrors the edge function's env-var lookup. The map is built
    # in config/runtime.exs / config/dev.exs from *_TRANSACTIONAL_ID env vars.
    # Only workshopRegistration has a real Loops ID as its fallback default;
    # the others must be configured or we fail fast (never send the friendly
    # name to Loops — that produces a 404 after 5 retries).
    map = Application.get_env(:dhc, :loops_transactional_ids, %{})

    case Map.get(map, to_string(friendly_name)) do
      nil ->
        Logger.error(
          "[email-worker] No Loops ID mapped for transactional_id",
          Keyword.merge(ctx, transactional_id: friendly_name)
        )

        Sentry.capture_message("Loops transactional ID not configured",
          level: :error,
          extra: %{
            transactional_id: friendly_name,
            oban_job_id: ctx[:oban_job_id],
            oban_attempt: ctx[:oban_attempt],
            oban_queue: ctx[:oban_queue],
            oban_worker: ctx[:oban_worker]
          }
        )

        {:error, {:transactional_id_not_configured, friendly_name}}

      loops_id when is_binary(loops_id) and loops_id != "" ->
        {:ok, loops_id}

      _ ->
        Logger.error(
          "[email-worker] Loops ID mapping is empty for transactional_id",
          Keyword.merge(ctx, transactional_id: friendly_name)
        )

        {:error, {:transactional_id_not_configured, friendly_name}}
    end
  end

  defp post_to_loops(
         %{"email" => email, "transactional_id" => transactional_id} = args,
         loops_id,
         ctx
       ) do
    api_key = loops_api_key()

    if is_nil(api_key) or api_key == "" do
      Logger.error(
        "[email-worker] LOOPS_API_KEY not configured",
        Keyword.merge(ctx, email: email, transactional_id: transactional_id)
      )

      {:error, :api_key_not_configured}
    else
      data_variables = Map.get(args, "data_variables", %{})

      payload = %{
        email: email,
        transactionalId: loops_id,
        dataVariables: data_variables
      }

      headers = [
        {"authorization", "Bearer #{api_key}"},
        {"content-type", "application/json"}
      ]

      Logger.debug(
        "[email-worker] POST to Loops",
        Keyword.merge(ctx,
          email: email,
          transactional_id: transactional_id,
          loops_id: loops_id,
          loops_url: loops_api_url(),
          data_variables: inspect(data_variables)
        )
      )

      case Req.post(loops_api_url(), json: payload, headers: headers) do
        {:ok, %Req.Response{status: status}} when status in 200..299 ->
          Logger.info(
            "[email-worker] Email sent successfully",
            Keyword.merge(ctx,
              email: email,
              transactional_id: transactional_id,
              loops_id: loops_id,
              loops_status: status
            )
          )

          :ok

        {:ok, %Req.Response{status: status} = response} ->
          Logger.error(
            "[email-worker] Loops API returned #{status}",
            Keyword.merge(ctx,
              email: email,
              transactional_id: transactional_id,
              loops_id: loops_id,
              loops_status: status,
              loops_body: inspect(response.body)
            )
          )

          {:error, {:loops_api, status}}

        {:error, exception} ->
          Logger.error(
            "[email-worker] HTTP request failed: #{inspect(exception)}",
            Keyword.merge(ctx,
              email: email,
              transactional_id: transactional_id,
              loops_id: loops_id,
              http_error: inspect(exception)
            )
          )

          {:error, {:http_error, exception}}
      end
    end
  end

  defp loops_api_key do
    Application.get_env(:dhc, :loops_api_key)
  end

  defp job_log_context(%Oban.Job{} = job) do
    [
      oban_job_id: job.id,
      oban_attempt: job.attempt,
      oban_queue: job.queue,
      oban_worker: job.worker
    ]
  end

defmodule Dhc.Email.DevMailer do
  @moduledoc """
  Relays non-prod email jobs to the local Mailpit container.

  In production, emails are rendered by Loops from its templates. In dev/test
  we don't have those templates, so each job's payload (recipient, friendly
  template name, data variables) is delivered as plain JSON instead — enough
  to verify who would receive what. Read the messages in the Mailpit web UI
  at `http://localhost:8025` (the `mailpit` service in the root
  `docker-compose.yml`, SMTP on `localhost:1025`).

  Swapped out in tests via the `:email_dev_mailer` app env (see
  `test/support/email_dev_mailer_stub.ex`), mirroring the
  `:discord_oauth_strategy` / `:onboarding_stripe_adapter` seams.

  ## Message format

  A minimal RFC 5322 message built by hand (CRLF line endings, base64 body so
  non-ASCII `data_variables` values stay 7-bit clean) — no `:mimemail`
  involved. Mailpit decodes and displays the JSON body as plain text.
  """

  require Logger

  @default_config [relay: "localhost", port: 1025, from: "dev@dhc.local"]

  @doc """
  Delivers `body` to `to` over SMTP via the configured dev relay.

  Returns `:ok` on delivery, or `{:error, reason}`. Callers decide how to
  react: the email worker logs and swallows failures so a stopped Mailpit
  container never wedges the dev Oban queue.
  """
  def deliver(to, subject, body) when is_binary(to) and is_binary(subject) and is_binary(body) do
    config = smtp_config()
    from = Keyword.fetch!(config, :from)

    message =
      [
        "From: #{from}",
        "To: #{to}",
        "Subject: #{subject}",
        "MIME-Version: 1.0",
        "Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8",
        "Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64",
        "",
        Base.encode64(body)
      ]
      |> Enum.join("\r\n")

    # Mailpit needs no auth or TLS; a short timeout keeps a wedged relay from
    # stalling an Oban worker for the client's long default.
    options = [
      relay: Keyword.fetch!(config, :relay),
      port: Keyword.fetch!(config, :port),
      auth: :never,
      tls: :never,
      timeout: 5_000
    ]

    case :gen_smtp_client.send_blocking({from, [to], message}, options) do
      receipt when is_binary(receipt) ->
        :ok

      {:error, _kind, reason} = error ->
        Logger.warning("[dev-mailer] SMTP delivery failed: #{inspect(reason)}")
        error

      {:error, reason} = error ->
        Logger.warning("[dev-mailer] SMTP delivery failed: #{inspect(reason)}")
        error
    end
  end

  defp smtp_config do
    Application.get_env(:dhc, :dev_smtp, @default_config)
  end
end

I'd need to verify Resend's Templates API supports programmatic update + publish before betting the pipeline on it.
- **(B) App-shipped HTML:** the package renders to static HTML/text artifacts that ship with (or beside) the Phoenix release; sends carry raw `html`. The provider becomes pure transport — "hide the email provider" is then literally true, and dev Mailpit shows real rendered emails from day one with zero provider involved. Cost: variable interpolation moves in-house — Elixir substitutes values into placeholders and must HTML-escape them (member display names flow into these emails; naive string replace is an injection bug).

Your stated goal is provider-hiding; (A) quietly violates it.

➡️ (B) app-shipped HTML with escaped placeholder substitution, CI just verifies artifacts are fresh.

---

❓ **Q3** - **Does the seam deserve its own behaviour at all?** Three options: (a) a `Dhc.Email.Adapter` behaviour with kind-level callbacks, mirroring `Dhc.Discord.Adapter`; (b) no new behaviour — Swoosh.Mailer *is* the seam: the Worker resolves kind → builds `%Swoosh.Email{}` → `Mailer.deliver/1`, provider chosen by runtime config, tests via `Swoosh.Adapters.Test`; (c) both layers. The Worker is already the stable semantic boundary callers use; a second behaviour beneath it may be ceremony. Discord.Adapter earns its existence because Nostrum is invasive; Swoosh is designed to be configured, not wrapped.

➡️ (b): kill DevMailer and the Bypass stubs, keep the Worker as the only domain-facing surface.

---

❓ **Q4** - **Confirm Swoosh despite the Req mandate?** You said Swoosh twice so I take it as leaning, but it contradicts a written convention, so it gets one explicit challenge. Honest framing: if Q2 lands on (B), the Resend send is one Req JSON POST (~Stripe.Client-shaped, ~100 lines) and Swoosh's residual value is the SMTP dev adapter (deleting your hand-rolled RFC 5322 code) plus test assertions. If Q2 lands on (A), Swoosh's `:template` option helps more. Swoosh costs: a framework dep, its own HTTP stack (point it at the already-present Finch via `Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch` to avoid pulling Hackney into prod), and an AGENTS.md/reach note documenting the exception.

➡️ Accept Swoosh, amend apps/phoenix/AGENTS.md with the exception, configure `Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch`.

---

❓ **Q5** - **Vocabulary: `transactional_id` is Loops jargon living in your job args.** You're building a provider-hiding seam while the domain's own name for its core concept names the incumbent vendor. Proposals for CONTEXT.md: **Transactional Email** (the message — distinct from in-app Notification), **Email Kind** (the code identifier behind the friendly-name whitelist: `magicLink`, `inviteMember`, …), **Template** (markup + metadata like subject/from). The wrinkle: `"transactional_id"` is serialized inside queued Oban jobs, so the wire key survives as a legacy alias read alongside the new name until drained.

➡️ Adopt Transactional Email / Email Kind / Template in the glossary; keep `transactional_id` as the job-arg serialization name, add the new key going forward.

---

❓ **Q6** - **Double-send window you already have:** no `Idempotency-Key` is sent today; a Loops timeout after successful send makes Oban retry a delivered email (max_attempts 5). Harmless-ish for magic links, annoying for workshop announcements. Both providers support the header with a 24h window; a deterministic key derived from the Oban job closes most of the gap for free during the rewrite.

➡️ Add `Idempotency-Key: oban-<job.id>` while rewriting the send path.

---

❓ **Q7** - **Scope guardrails.** Webhooks (delivery events), attachments, scheduled sends, batch endpoint, audience/contact sync: none used today. The research doc shows each is a provider-differences minefield. Confirm all stay out of scope so neither the seam nor the templates package grows speculative surface — revisit webhooks post-migration only if bounced magic links become a visible problem.

➡️ All out of scope for this effort.

---

Answer what you like, push back anywhere — your answers settle branches and I'll recompute the frontier, write resolved terms into CONTEXT.md as we go, and offer ADRs (0021+) where a decision is hard to reverse, surprising, and a real trade-off (Q2 and Q4 are already shaping up as ADR material).

 | Term | Definition |

 | **Member** | A person with a club membership. Owns club profile facts such as identity, contact data, and preferred weapon. Its `user_profiles.principal_id` links to the DHC-owned Phoenix Authentication Principal. |
 | **Authentication Principal** | The DHC-owned login identity for exactly one Member. It owns the authoritative login email and may have login methods such as magic link or linked External Identities. A principal may establish a Session only while its Member has club access; pending Invitations do not yet have principals. A Principal links to exactly one UserProfile via `user_profiles.principal_id` (unique), and exactly one MemberProfile via `member_profiles.id` (which equals the Principal ID); database constraints enforce that both links refer to the same Principal, preventing linkage drift. |
 | **External Identity** | An account at an external identity provider that is explicitly linked to one Authentication Principal. Its immutable provider subject, not its reported email or username, establishes the link. A principal has at most one identity per provider, and an external account cannot belong to multiple principals. |
 | **Staged Discord Assignment** | A hand-made, unproven mapping from an existing Member's Authentication Principal to one Discord provider subject, produced by a one-off manual matching of the guild roster against Members and inserted directly into production. It is not an External Identity or login capability: only its first matching Discord OAuth proof atomically promotes it to the External Identity. User ID is the binding fact; the stored username snapshot is matching metadata only. The staging/review pipeline that exists in code (proposed → approved/rejected/withdrawn/superseded) was never exercised in production — no reviewed, rejected, or approved rows exist; production rows are simply unconsumed until promoted. |
 | **Session** | A revocable, per-device authenticated relationship between a browser and an Authentication Principal. A valid Session implies that the associated Member currently has club access; identity proof without club access is not an authenticated dashboard Session. Loss of club access revokes all Sessions, so restored access requires a fresh sign-in rather than reactivating an old Session. |
 | **Membership** | A recurring subscription/access relationship managed via Stripe. Owns subscription and access state such as `active`, `inactive`, or `paused`, pause-until dates, and Stripe customer/subscription linkage. An inactive Membership means the member has no active subscription. |
 | **isActive** | A projection of Membership subscription state onto `user_profiles.is_active`, written by the Stripe webhook — a member is active iff they have club access, including a paused Membership. It is NOT independently admin-settable; there is no API endpoint that writes it. Stripe is the source of truth; a missed webhook leaves the projection stale (drift risk). A Member must be active to establish or continue an authenticated dashboard Session. Distinct from `membershipStatus`, which also encodes `paused`. |
 | **Paused** | A Membership status where `subscription_paused_until` is in the future. The Member retains access (`isActive = true`) but is not charged. |
 | **Workshop** | A scheduled club activity with date, capacity, authoritative Member and external-attendee pricing, and Registration. The Workshop's price determines the amount charged; callers do not supply charge amounts. Use Workshop in domain language; `club_activity_*` is persistence vocabulary. |
 | **Registration** | An attendee's sign-up for a Workshop. A Member Registration belongs to a Member; an external Registration belongs to an attendee snapshot. A cancelled or refunded Registration is a closed chapter; it stays as historical record but no longer blocks a fresh Registration for the same attendee and Workshop. Uniqueness is enforced only among active Registrations (pending or confirmed); multiple historical rows per attendee and Workshop are permitted. Every valid paid Payment Attempt concludes with either a Registration or automatic compensation through a Refund; payments with invalid or mismatched identity remain policy failures. |
 | **Payment Attempt** | The durable identity of an attempt to pay for a Workshop Registration. It records the Workshop, attendee, authoritative amount and currency, payment method, and provider identity. Replays resume the same Payment Attempt. Once validly paid, it concludes exactly once with either a Registration or a compensating Refund. |
 | **Refund** | A durable, cancellation-triggered or compensation-triggered repayment workflow tracked in `club_activity_refunds`. A Refund may repay a retained Registration or a paid Payment Attempt that could not produce one. Creating a Refund records the obligation; Stripe acceptance and terminal completion happen asynchronously. Transport and provider failures retry with stable idempotency, while validation and policy failures require intervention. Stripe events advance Refunds promptly and reconciliation repairs missed events. |
 | **Retention Policy** | Financial and audit records (Registrations, Refunds, inventory history) are retained permanently — `ON DELETE RESTRICT` prevents destroying them when a parent is removed. Workshops with Registrations and Members are soft-deleted (archived), never hard-deleted; a Member may be anonymized or detached from personal data without destroying transactional records. Workshops with zero Registrations, empty containers, unused equipment categories, inventory items, orphaned notifications, expired/revoked Invitations, and external users with zero Registrations may be hard-deleted. Registrations carry an attendee snapshot (display name, email) captured at transaction time so profile anonymization does not corrupt event and payment history. The inventory-history retention clause (`ON DELETE SET NULL` so items can be hard-deleted while history survives) is target-state, not yet enforced — deferred until the equipment domain goes production-ready. |
 | **Inventory** | Club equipment (swords, masks, etc.) tracked in containers/categories with movement history. |
 | **Invitation** | A pending or processed invite for a prospective member. At most one pending Invitation exists per canonical email at any time; expired, accepted, or revoked Invitations accumulate as history and do not block reissue. Each pending Invitation carries a pre-allocated Principal UUID (its `prospective_principal_id`) used at acceptance; a fresh UUID per issue avoids conflict. |
 | **Invitation Acceptance** | The atomic Onboarding conversion event where a prospective member accepts an Invitation and becomes a Principal, Member, Stripe-backed Membership, Role holder, and verified Discord External Identity in one database transaction. Complimentary membership uses the existing 100% discount mechanism rather than a separate acceptance path. Issue time records only the Invitation; acceptance creates the Principal, `UserProfile`, `MemberProfile`, and `member` Role together, keyed by `invitation.prospective_principal_id`. The prospective member must prove control of the Discord account during acceptance; that account's immutable provider subject, not its mutable username or reported email, binds it to the new Principal. When the invitee has an existing Waitlist UserProfile, acceptance claims and activates that profile (setting `principal_id`, `is_active`) rather than creating a duplicate; guardian linkage and intake-captured fields (gender, pronouns, medical conditions) carry over. For direct Invitations without a Waitlist entry, a new profile is created. Invitation credentials and Discord OAuth must be verified before payment progression starts. Acceptance is the registration; it never establishes a Session. |
 | **Invitation Acceptance Attempt** | A durable record of one attempt to perform Invitation Acceptance. At most one active Attempt exists per Invitation; retries resume it rather than creating another. A declined Attempt must close before another may begin. It exists before Stripe work, records external progress and failure independently, and survives rollback of Principal and Member creation so an operator or retry can reconcile residual Stripe state. It does not weaken the atomic conversion of the prospective member into a Principal and Member. |
 | **Invitation Acceptance Discord Continuation** | A short-lived, invitation- and Attempt-bound proof that the prospective member passed Invitation credential verification and Discord OAuth. It temporarily carries the Discord provider subject and mutable display metadata but is neither an External Identity nor a login capability. Its active subject claim prevents concurrent bindings of the same Discord account; its raw subject is removed when it expires, fails, or is consumed. |
 | **Discord Subject Claim** | A short-lived, subject-only reservation owned by a verified Invitation Acceptance Discord Continuation. It has no Principal and is deleted when the Continuation ends or atomically becomes an External Identity. It prevents a Staged Discord Assignment or any other binding path from using the same Discord account mid-acceptance. |
 | **Discord Join Grant** | A short-lived custody record for the Discord user access token collected (with the `guilds.join` scope) during Invitation Acceptance Discord OAuth. It exists solely so the bot can add the new Member to the guild after conversion commits; it is encrypted at rest, is never a login capability, and its token is zeroized once the guild join succeeds, terminally fails, or the token expires. It is the only place the system ever holds a member OAuth credential. |
 | **Onboarding** | The end-to-end journey from prospective member intake through invitation acceptance and member record creation. Waitlist is the intake side of Onboarding; Invitations are the conversion side. |
 | **Notification** | A per-user in-app message generated by the system. Ordered by creation time and unread until `readAt` is set; users only see their own notifications. |
+| **Transactional Email** | An outbound email sent to one recipient as the side effect of a workflow event (sign-in, invitation issue, registration, announcement). Distinct from Notification, which is in-app only. Sending is asynchronous: the workflow enqueues it and never blocks on delivery success. |
+| **Email Kind** | The stable, provider-neutral identifier selecting one Transactional Email type (`inviteMember`, `magicLink`, …). Callers reference only the Kind and its data variables; how a Kind resolves to a concrete provider-side template is send-path concern, never caller vocabulary. |
+| **Template** | The owned-as-code source of an Email Kind's content: markup plus metadata (subject, sender, declared typed variables). Published to the provider's template store; the published copy is what renders variables at send time. |
 | **Waitlist** | Prospective members awaiting invitation. A distinct domain area within Onboarding, not merely part of Member management. |
 | **Waitlist Status** | The stage of a prospective member on the waitlist: waiting, invited, paid, deferred, cancelled, completed, no_reply, or joined. |
 | **Settings** | Cross-domain or system-wide configuration that is managed as configuration rather than as part of a specific domain workflow. A value stored in the settings table is not automatically a Settings capability concern; domain-owned values such as Waitlist availability should be exposed through their owning domain language. |
 | **Role** | An authorization level assigned to a user. Drawn from `role_type` enum (admin, president, member, committee roles). |
 | **Discord Doctor** | The admin capability that reconciles Member records against the Discord guild roster: every human guild account lands in exactly one bucket — Linked–active (healthy), Linked–inactive (kickable, bulk-kickable), Pending link (matches an unconsumed Staged Discord Assignment; shows the believed Member and their membership status), or Unrecognized (no live match; kickable, bulk-kickable) — plus a report-only Members view of who is missing from the guild (with an auto-join-pending badge for fresh acceptances) or never linked. It supports manual, human-reviewed kicks (never bans, never automatic). Kicks leave no record in the system: the guild's own Discord audit log — which attributes every kick to the bot, so its generated reason string names the driving administrator and the target's bucket — is the only trace, and its limited retention is accepted. Pending links are kickable, but only one-by-one with an explicit "unconfirmed match — verify on Discord first" warning — never in bulk kicks. Members holding any Role beyond plain member are kick-proof (shown as protected). Bot accounts are excluded from the roster.  ## Test Harness Language
 
 | Term | Definition |
 |------|-----------|
 | **Test Harness** | The automated execution environment for a given suite. Distinct from the data it runs against. Two harnesses exist: the Phoenix (Elixir) harness and the Playwright (E2E) harness. |
 | **Characterization Test** | A test that pins the *current* behavior of an affected code path before a migration changes it — even if that behavior is defective. Written first, it goes red when the fix lands (confirming the behavior changed); a companion test asserting the *desired* behavior then goes green. Required before any schema-migration ticket that touches an untested path, per the audit finding that moduledoc-claimed behavior is often not asserted by any test. |
 | **Test Fixture** | The per-test setup data. Inserted and torn down by the test itself, not the harness. |
 | **Postgres Surface** | The minimal dependency for the Phoenix harness: a Postgres container plus a seeded `auth` schema (GoTrue-owned tables such as `auth.users`). No HTTP services. |
 | **Supabase Surface** | The full dependency for the E2E harness: Kong + GoTrue + PostgREST + Postgres. Required because E2E seeds/teardowns via the Supabase HTTP API and derives the auth cookie name from the project ref host. |
 | **Auth Schema Bootstrap** | The `auth` schema DDL the Phoenix harness relies on. The `supabase/postgres:17.6.1.136` image already ships `00000000000001-auth-schema.sql` at container init, creating the full `auth.users` table, `auth.schema_migrations`, and the `supabase_auth_admin` role. No bespoke bootstrap file is needed; the image is the bootstrap. GoTrue's own migrations run `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, so in the `supabase` profile GoTrue boots cleanly against the image-seeded table. |
 | **Shared Container** | A single testcontainer started once per `mix test` run (in `test_helper.exs`) and shared across all test cases via the Ecto SQL Sandbox. Distinct from per-test isolation (which the sandbox provides) and from per-test-case containers (rejected as too slow). |
 | **Compose-Driven Harness** | Both test harnesses drive the same stripped Supabase `docker-compose.yml` via `Testcontainers.DockerCompose` (Phoenix) and `docker compose` CLI (E2E). The compose file is the single source of truth for the stack shape; profiles gate which services each harness starts. |
 | **Per-Run Lifecycle** | The Phoenix harness does a full compose `up` at `mix test` start and `down -v` on `System.at_exit`. No cross-run reuse — every run starts from a freshly migrated DB with the Auth Schema Bootstrap applied. Deterministic at the cost of ~2-4s cold start; reuse is a deferred optimization. |
 | **Migration Deploy Shape** | Schema migrations run at deploy time via the Fly release command. Additive migrations (new indexes, nullable columns, non-conflicting CHECK constraints) deploy routinely. Destructive or non-splittable changes (column type changes, citext casts, index drops that change uniqueness semantics) use expand-contract where possible (expand → backfill → contract) and a maintenance window with write freeze for the contract step or for changes that cannot be split. Each migration ticket declares its deploy shape so the operator knows which require coordination. |
 | **E2E Deferral** | The Playwright harness E2E migration is out of scope for the current work. Only Phoenix is being reworked now. The compose file shape must support E2E later (profiles, Kong/GoTrue/PostgREST), but E2E's fixed-port and cookie-derivation concerns are deferred. |
 | **Uniform Profiles** | Every service in the stripped compose file carries a `profiles:` entry — `db` for Postgres (+ Auth Schema Bootstrap), `supabase` for GoTrue/Kong/PostgREST. No default-always services. Phoenix starts with `with_profile("db")`; E2E will later start with `with_profile("supabase")` (and `with_profile("db")` if it needs the DB too).
 | **Ephemeral DB Volume** | The Phoenix harness runs the `db` service with no persistent `PGDATA` volume — `down -v` on `System.at_exit` destroys all data. Fresh container, fresh migration, fresh `auth` schema per `mix test` run. No upstream Supabase init-SQL mounts are needed; the `supabase/postgres` image already ships `auth.users` and `pg_jsonschema`. |
 | **Root Compose File** | The stripped Supabase `docker-compose.yml` lives at the repo root next to the existing root `.env`. This lets Compose's built-in `.env` resolution interpolate `${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}` etc. without plumbing env vars through `DockerCompose.with_env/3` or duplicating the env file. testcontainers-elixir's `DockerCompose.new/1` sets `cd` to the compose file's directory, so a root-level file means `cd: repo_root` where `.env` already sits. | |
 
 ## Migration State
 
 - **Phase 1a**: Edge functions → Oban (in progress)
 - **Phase 1b**: Service layer → Phoenix API (next)
 - **Phase 2**: LiveView migration (future evaluation)
 
 Supabase-hosted Postgres and Storage remain in place throughout Phase 1. Phoenix owns authentication through generated Principals, magic links, opaque database-backed Sessions, and Assent Discord OAuth. M2 repointed application ownership and foreign keys to `principals.id`; Supabase `auth.*` remains only as rollback dead weight during observation and until the separate Postgres-hosting migration. PostgREST and RLS policies are removed when all data access is proxied through Phoenix.

parts.text:
The staging grep: "staging" only appears in discord/assignments.ex (unrelated — that's the Staged Discord Assignment concept). Config has config.exs, dev.exs, prod.exs, runtime.exs, test.exs — no staging.exs. So there is **no staging environment**; environments are dev/test/prod. That sharpens the cutover question: rehearsal happens in dev against Resend's sandbox (resend.dev, own-email-only) or a test domain.

CONTEXT.md updated with the three terms. Now compose round 2 of the frontier.

What's settled:
- Q1: Order = seam → templates package → single cutover
- Q2: Resend-hosted templates, code-authored, CLI/CI-uploaded (VERIFIED feasible + alias support)
- Q3: Swoosh IS the seam, no bespoke behaviour
- Q4: Swoosh + Finch api client, AGENTS.md amendment
- Q5: Vocabulary adopted (written to CONTEXT.md)
- Q6: Idempotency-Key oban-<job.id>
- Q7: Webhooks/attachments/scheduling/batch/audiences out of scope

New verified facts to report:
1. Official `resend` CLI exists with full templates CRUD + publish; CI-friendly (RESEND_API_KEY env var, JSON output).
2. **Templates API supports `alias`** — create accepts alias; update/delete work by ID **or alias**; sends accept alias in the template id field (`template: {id: 'order-confirmation'}`). → deterministic kind→alias addressing possible; no env-var ID map needed.
3. Templates carry default `from` and `subject`, overridable at send time → subject/sender authored in code.
4. Draft→publish lifecycle: update creates draft; publish makes live; version history; already-sent unaffected.
5. Variables: ≤20 per template, typed string|number, optional fallback_value, reserved names; missing-without-fallback fails at send. Matches today's data_variables constraint exactly.
6. React Email integration exists (`react-email resend setup`, preview-server Upload/Bulk Upload) but needs Full Access key and is interactive — for CI/CD the plain CLI/API is the right tool.

Round 2 frontier questions:

**Q8 — Template addressing**: alias-based vs env-var ID map.
(a) Alias-addressed sends: each Email Kind maps mechanically to a template alias (verbatim camelCase or kebab-case); worker sends `template.id = alias`. No env vars, no runtime resolution, kills `{:transactional_id_not_configured}` failure mode. Risk: typo'd alias surfaces as send-time validation error → mitigated by a smoke test/startup check listing published templates.
(b) Status-quo shape: sync writes generated IDs into env vars/fnox, worker resolves via config map.
Rec: (a), kebab-case aliases (`invite-member`) with one mechanical transform — or verbatim camelCase for zero transform? Resend example uses kebab (`order-confirmation`). Alias charset constraints unverified — flag implementation-time check. I'll recommend kebab-case with mechanical translation, since it matches provider convention and avoids any case-sensitivity surprises... actually zero-transform (verbatim kind name) is simpler and the whitelist already guards typos at enqueue time. Hmm. The worker validates kinds against @transactional_ids whitelist BEFORE sending, so an unknown kind never reaches the API. Alias == kind verbatim means zero translation logic. I'll recommend verbatim with fallback note.

**Q9 — Non-prod rendering story**: what lands in Mailpit?
(a) Status quo+: text summary of kind+vars in the email body (current behavior, ported into Swoosh-shaped builder)
(b) Local real renders: react-email preview server for authoring DX (`pnpm emails dev` hot reload); Mailpit stays summary-only
(c) Build HTML snapshots consumed by dev mailer — reintroduces local interpolation machinery; rejected complexity
Rec: (a)+(b). Also note: Swoosh.Adapters.Mailpit is HTTP-based → gen_smtp dep droppable.

Wait — is Swoosh.Adapters.Mailpit HTTP or SMTP? Research doc README quote lists "MailPit" among adapters. Mailpit has both SMTP (1025) and HTTP API (8025). Swoosh's Mailpit adapter uses the HTTP API I believe. Either way works with existing docker-compose service. Don't overclaim — say "Swoosh ships a Mailpit adapter; whether it lets us drop gen_smtp gets checked at implementation."

**Q10 — Sync pipeline mechanics**:
Tooling options: official CLI script (upsert by alias + publish, --json, RESEND_API_KEY env) vs react-email preview-server interactive upload vs bespoke API script in package.
Trigger: merge-to-main auto-publish vs manual dispatch/local command vs PR-drafts+main-publish.
Key: Full Access required (templates API rejects send-only keys per react-email guide; send-only key restriction from research doc §2). CI secret storage.
Rec: scripted sync in the package using official CLI semantics (create-or-update by alias, then publish), run manually at first (`mise run email-sync` style or pnpm script), CI job on merge-to-main once trusted; dashboard edits treated as drift overwritten next sync; version history is the safety net.

**Q11 — Package naming + variable schema ownership**: 
Name: packages/email-templates (rec). Contents: emails/*.tsx + manifest metadata (exported from component files or central manifest.ts: subject, from, variables with types/fallbacks).
Schema source of truth: TS types per kind; Elixir keeps generic string|number validation; Resend enforces declared requirements at send.
Rec: yes.

**Q12 — Cutover mechanics + rehearsal venue**: No staging environment exists (verified: config has only dev/test/prod). Options:
(a) Global flip rehearsed in dev against Resend sandbox (from onboarding@resend.dev → own account email only) + prod flip with Loops creds kept warm for instant rollback
(b) Per-kind routing table (kind→provider) enabling incremental migration — more machinery
Rec: (a). At 5 kinds and club scale, global flip with warm rollback beats routing machinery. magicLink is auth-critical: flip during low-activity window; monitor Sentry/Oban discard rates.

**Q13 — Error classification**: today every non-2xx retries 5×. Under Resend: deterministic validation errors (missing variable without fallback, unknown template alias, unverified domain 403) will NEVER succeed on retry → should discard + Sentry instead of burning attempts; transient (429 w/ Retry-After, 5xx, network) → retry with backoff. Idempotency key already adopted (Q6 round 1).
Rec: classify in the seam; validation-family failures cancel the job.

Also ADR offers: two qualify now —
0021 Swoosh-as-seam (amends Req mandate; Finch api_client)
0022 Code-authored templates synced to Resend-hosted store over CI/CD
I'll offer them and write after this round's answers fold in (or now if user says go).

Format: report facts compactly first, then questions in the skill format. Keep tight — user gives terse answers, don't bury them.

CONTEXT.md now carries **Transactional Email**, **Email Kind**, and **Template**. And the fact-check matters: there's no staging environment (`config/` holds only dev/test/prod) — that shapes the cutover question below.

**Your Q2 claim verified, plus three bonuses that simplify the design:**

1. ✅ Official `resend` CLI exists (`resend templates list/create/update/delete/duplicate/publish`), auth via `RESEND_API_KEY`, JSON output, built for CI/CD.
2. 🎁 **Templates have stable aliases.** Create accepts an `alias`; update/delete work "by ID or alias"; and sends accept the alias directly in the template id field (`template: {id: "order-confirmation"}`). This can delete your entire kind→ID config map — no `*_TRANSACTIONAL_ID`-style env vars ever again.
3. 🎁 **Templates carry `subject` and `from` defaults**, authored at upload time, overridable per-send. So subject/sender identity live in the React components, not Elixir config.
4. 🎁 **Draft→publish lifecycle with version history**: updates land as drafts until published; published edits never touch already-sent mail. Variables: ≤20 per template, typed `string|number` (exactly today's constraint), optional fallback, missing-without-fallback fails at send.

One caveat: the interactive path (`react-email resend setup` + preview-server Upload button) needs a **Full Access** key and is manual — fine locally, not for CI. The plain CLI/API is the sync tool.

Round 2 frontier:

---

❓ **Q8** - **Address templates by alias, killing the ID-map config entirely?** With aliases verified: (a) the Worker addresses `template.id` by a mechanical function of the Email Kind (e.g. `inviteMember` → `invite-member`, or verbatim), so zero env vars, zero runtime resolution, and the `{:transactional_id_not_configured, ...}` failure mode ceases to exist; the sync pipeline guarantees the alias exists. Risk: a typo'd alias surfaces only as a send-time validation error — mitigated by the compile-time kind whitelist plus a staging-style smoke check that lists published templates. (b) Keep today's shape: sync writes Resend UUIDs into env vars, worker resolves through a config map.

➡️ (a), alias = kebab-case of the Kind, enforced by one shared naming module; add a cheap test asserting every whitelisted Kind has a published template.

---

❓ **Q9** - **What does non-prod actually render, given hosted templates?** Today Mailpit receives the raw JSON payload because nothing local can render. Options: (a) keep that — a text summary of Kind + variables, accurately representing what prod hands Resend; authoring previews happen separately via `react-email dev` (hot-reload preview server, zero plumbing); (b) build placeholder-laden HTML snapshots locally so Mailpit shows near-real emails — but that drags interpolation machinery into Elixir, the exact complexity we just rejected in favor of hosted rendering; (c) dev/staging hits the Resend sandbox live — network + key + recipient restrictions in everyday dev.

➡️ (a) + `react-email dev` for visual work. Bonus: Swoosh ships a Mailpit adapter, likely letting us drop `gen_smtp` too — checked at implementation.

---

❓ **Q10** - **Who runs the upload, when?** The publish step changes production emails, including the auth-critical magic link. Options: (a) merge-to-main auto-sync (upsert-by-alias + publish): fully automated, drift-proof, but a bad merge republishes prod templates instantly; (b) manual trigger first (`pnpm emails sync` locally or `workflow_dispatch`), graduate to auto-publish once trust builds — draft/publish version history is the safety net either way; (c) PRs always upload as drafts, main publishes. Requires a Full Access key wherever it runs (send-only keys can't manage templates).

➡️ (c)-shaped: CI uploads drafts on every PR, publishes on merge to main — automation you wanted, with the risky step still gated on the merge event, not arbitrary pushes.

---

❓ **Q11** - **Package shape:** name it `packages/email-templates`; contents are `emails/*.tsx` React Email components where each file exports its metadata (subject default, from default, declared variables with types/fallbacks) alongside the component — TypeScript stays the single schema authority for what each Kind requires; Elixir keeps only its generic string|number check and lets Resend enforce per-template contracts at send.

➡️ Yes, as stated.

---

❓ **Q12** - **Cutover mechanics with no staging environment:** (a) global flip — one config change swaps the Swoosh adapter from Loops to Resend; rehearsed in dev against the sandbox (which only delivers to your own account address until the domain verifies), then flipped in prod with Loops credentials left warm for instant rollback; (b) per-kind routing table so kinds migrate one at a time — finer control, permanent extra machinery.

➡️ (a). Five kinds, club scale: a global flip in a quiet window plus warm rollback beats building routing infrastructure you'll delete after week one.

---

❓ **Q13** - **Stop retrying deterministic failures.** Today *every* non-2xx triggers 5 Oban attempts. Under Resend, a missing variable without fallback or an unknown alias can never succeed on retry — re-attempts are pure noise. Classify at the seam: validation-family failures (4xx semantic errors) → discard immediately + Sentry; rate limits (429) → retry respecting backoff; 5xx/network → retry.

➡️ Adopt the classification while rewriting the send path.

---

Answer these six and the tree is done — then I'll draft ADRs 0021 (Swoosh as the email transport seam, amending the Req mandate) and 0022 (code-authored templates synced to Resend's hosted store over CI/CD), which both meet the hard-to-reverse / surprising / real-trade-off bar.

 # CONTEXT: DHC Dashboard
 
 **Last updated:** 2026-08-22
 **Status:** Active migration from SvelteKit + Supabase + Deno edge functions to Phoenix + Ecto + Oban
 
 ## Domain Language
 
 | Term | Definition |
 |------|-----------|
 | **Member** | A person with a club membership. Owns club profile facts such as identity, contact data, and preferred weapon. Its `user_profiles.principal_id` links to the DHC-owned Phoenix Authentication Principal. |
 | **Authentication Principal** | The DHC-owned login identity for exactly one Member. It owns the authoritative login email and may have login methods such as magic link or linked External Identities. A principal may establish a Session only while its Member has club access; pending Invitations do not yet have principals. A Principal links to exactly one UserProfile via `user_profiles.principal_id` (unique), and exactly one MemberProfile via `member_profiles.id` (which equals the Principal ID); database constraints enforce that both links refer to the same Principal, preventing linkage drift. |
 | **External Identity** | An account at an external identity provider that is explicitly linked to one Authentication Principal. Its immutable provider subject, not its reported email or username, establishes the link. A principal has at most one identity per provider, and an external account cannot belong to multiple principals. |
 | **Staged Discord Assignment** | A hand-made, unproven mapping from an existing Member's Authentication Principal to one Discord provider subject, produced by a one-off manual matching of the guild roster against Members and inserted directly into production. It is not an External Identity or login capability: only its first matching Discord OAuth proof atomically promotes it to the External Identity. User ID is the binding fact; the stored username snapshot is matching metadata only. The staging/review pipeline that exists in code (proposed → approved/rejected/withdrawn/superseded) was never exercised in production — no reviewed, rejected, or approved rows exist; production rows are simply unconsumed until promoted. |
 | **Session** | A revocable, per-device authenticated relationship between a browser and an Authentication Principal. A valid Session implies that the associated Member currently has club access; identity proof without club access is not an authenticated dashboard Session. Loss of club access revokes all Sessions, so restored access requires a fresh sign-in rather than reactivating an old Session. |
 | **Membership** | A recurring subscription/access relationship managed via Stripe. Owns subscription and access state such as `active`, `inactive`, or `paused`, pause-until dates, and Stripe customer/subscription linkage. An inactive Membership means the member has no active subscription. |
 | **isActive** | A projection of Membership subscription state onto `user_profiles.is_active`, written by the Stripe webhook — a member is active iff they have club access, including a paused Membership. It is NOT independently admin-settable; there is no API endpoint that writes it. Stripe is the source of truth; a missed webhook leaves the projection stale (drift risk). A Member must be active to establish or continue an authenticated dashboard Session. Distinct from `membershipStatus`, which also encodes `paused`. |
 | **Paused** | A Membership status where `subscription_paused_until` is in the future. The Member retains access (`isActive = true`) but is not charged. |
 | **Workshop** | A scheduled club activity with date, capacity, authoritative Member and external-attendee pricing, and Registration. The Workshop's price determines the amount charged; callers do not supply charge amounts. Use Workshop in domain language; `club_activity_*` is persistence vocabulary. |
 | **Registration** | An attendee's sign-up for a Workshop. A Member Registration belongs to a Member; an external Registration belongs to an attendee snapshot. A cancelled or refunded Registration is a closed chapter; it stays as historical record but no longer blocks a fresh Registration for the same attendee and Workshop. Uniqueness is enforced only among active Registrations (pending or confirmed); multiple historical rows per attendee and Workshop are permitted. Every valid paid Payment Attempt concludes with either a Registration or automatic compensation through a Refund; payments with invalid or mismatched identity remain policy failures. |
 | **Payment Attempt** | The durable identity of an attempt to pay for a Workshop Registration. It records the Workshop, attendee, authoritative amount and currency, payment method, and provider identity. Replays resume the same Payment Attempt. Once validly paid, it concludes exactly once with either a Registration or a compensating Refund. |
 | **Refund** | A durable, cancellation-triggered or compensation-triggered repayment workflow tracked in `club_activity_refunds`. A Refund may repay a retained Registration or a paid Payment Attempt that could not produce one. Creating a Refund records the obligation; Stripe acceptance and terminal completion happen asynchronously. Transport and provider failures retry with stable idempotency, while validation and policy failures require intervention. Stripe events advance Refunds promptly and reconciliation repairs missed events. |
 | **Retention Policy** | Financial and audit records (Registrations, Refunds, inventory history) are retained permanently — `ON DELETE RESTRICT` prevents destroying them when a parent is removed. Workshops with Registrations and Members are soft-deleted (archived), never hard-deleted; a Member may be anonymized or detached from personal data without destroying transactional records. Workshops with zero Registrations, empty containers, unused equipment categories, inventory items, orphaned notifications, expired/revoked Invitations, and external users with zero Registrations may be hard-deleted. Registrations carry an attendee snapshot (display name, email) captured at transaction time so profile anonymization does not corrupt event and payment history. The inventory-history retention clause (`ON DELETE SET NULL` so items can be hard-deleted while history survives) is target-state, not yet enforced — deferred until the equipment domain goes production-ready. |
 | **Inventory** | Club equipment (swords, masks, etc.) tracked in containers/categories with movement history. |
 | **Invitation** | A pending or processed invite for a prospective member. At most one pending Invitation exists per canonical email at any time; expired, accepted, or revoked Invitations accumulate as history and do not block reissue. Each pending Invitation carries a pre-allocated Principal UUID (its `prospective_principal_id`) used at acceptance; a fresh UUID per issue avoids conflict. |
 | **Invitation Acceptance** | The atomic Onboarding conversion event where a prospective member accepts an Invitation and becomes a Principal, Member, Stripe-backed Membership, Role holder, and verified Discord External Identity in one database transaction. Complimentary membership uses the existing 100% discount mechanism rather than a separate acceptance path. Issue time records only the Invitation; acceptance creates the Principal, `UserProfile`, `MemberProfile`, and `member` Role together, keyed by `invitation.prospective_principal_id`. The prospective member must prove control of the Discord account during acceptance; that account's immutable provider subject, not its mutable username or reported email, binds it to the new Principal. When the invitee has an existing Waitlist UserProfile, acceptance claims and activates that profile (setting `principal_id`, `is_active`) rather than creating a duplicate; guardian linkage and intake-captured fields (gender, pronouns, medical conditions) carry over. For direct Invitations without a Waitlist entry, a new profile is created. Invitation credentials and Discord OAuth must be verified before payment progression starts. Acceptance is the registration; it never establishes a Session. |
 | **Invitation Acceptance Attempt** | A durable record of one attempt to perform Invitation Acceptance. At most one active Attempt exists per Invitation; retries resume it rather than creating another. A declined Attempt must close before another may begin. It exists before Stripe work, records external progress and failure independently, and survives rollback of Principal and Member creation so an operator or retry can reconcile residual Stripe state. It does not weaken the atomic conversion of the prospective member into a Principal and Member. |
 | **Invitation Acceptance Discord Continuation** | A short-lived, invitation- and Attempt-bound proof that the prospective member passed Invitation credential verification and Discord OAuth. It temporarily carries the Discord provider subject and mutable display metadata but is neither an External Identity nor a login capability. Its active subject claim prevents concurrent bindings of the same Discord account; its raw subject is removed when it expires, fails, or is consumed. |
 | **Discord Subject Claim** | A short-lived, subject-only reservation owned by a verified Invitation Acceptance Discord Continuation. It has no Principal and is deleted when the Continuation ends or atomically becomes an External Identity. It prevents a Staged Discord Assignment or any other binding path from using the same Discord account mid-acceptance. |
 | **Discord Join Grant** | A short-lived custody record for the Discord user access token collected (with the `guilds.join` scope) during Invitation Acceptance Discord OAuth. It exists solely so the bot can add the new Member to the guild after conversion commits; it is encrypted at rest, is never a login capability, and its token is zeroized once the guild join succeeds, terminally fails, or the token expires. It is the only place the system ever holds a member OAuth credential. |
 | **Onboarding** | The end-to-end journey from prospective member intake through invitation acceptance and member record creation. Waitlist is the intake side of Onboarding; Invitations are the conversion side. |
 | **Notification** | A per-user in-app message generated by the system. Ordered by creation time and unread until `readAt` is set; users only see their own notifications. |
 | **Transactional Email** | An outbound email sent to one recipient as the side effect of a workflow event (sign-in, invitation issue, registration, announcement). Distinct from Notification, which is in-app only. Sending is asynchronous: the workflow enqueues it and never blocks on delivery success. |
 | **Email Kind** | The stable, provider-neutral identifier selecting one Transactional Email type (`inviteMember`, `magicLink`, …). Callers reference only the Kind and its data variables; how a Kind resolves to a concrete provider-side template is send-path concern, never caller vocabulary. |
 | **Template** | The owned-as-code source of an Email Kind's content: markup plus metadata (subject, sender, declared typed variables). Published to the provider's template store; the published copy is what renders variables at send time. |
 | **Waitlist** | Prospective members awaiting invitation. A distinct domain area within Onboarding, not merely part of Member management. |
 | **Waitlist Status** | The stage of a prospective member on the waitlist: waiting, invited, paid, deferred, cancelled, completed, no_reply, or joined. |
 | **Settings** | Cross-domain or system-wide configuration that is managed as configuration rather than as part of a specific domain workflow. A value stored in the settings table is not automatically a Settings capability concern; domain-owned values such as Waitlist availability should be exposed through their owning domain language. |
 | **Role** | An authorization level assigned to a user. Drawn from `role_type` enum (admin, president, member, committee roles). |
 | **Discord Doctor** | The admin capability that reconciles Member records against the Discord guild roster: every human guild account lands in exactly one bucket — Linked–active (healthy), Linked–inactive (kickable, bulk-kickable), Pending link (matches an unconsumed Staged Discord Assignment; shows the believed Member and their membership status), or Unrecognized (no live match; kickable, bulk-kickable) — plus a report-only Members view of who is missing from the guild (with an auto-join-pending badge for fresh acceptances) or never linked. It supports manual, human-reviewed kicks (never bans, never automatic). Kicks leave no record in the system: the guild's own Discord audit log — which attributes every kick to the bot, so its generated reason string names the driving administrator and the target's bucket — is the only trace, and its limited retention is accepted. Pending links are kickable, but only one-by-one with an explicit "unconfirmed match — verify on Discord first" warning — never in bulk kicks. Members holding any Role beyond plain member are kick-proof (shown as protected). Bot accounts are excluded from the roster. Members missing from the guild are reported only; re-connecting them happens manually outside the system (e.g. an admin DMs an invite link) — the Doctor sends no invites, and Onboarding's auto-join is the only in-system path into the guild. |

 | Term | Definition |
 |------|-----------|
 | **Test Harness** | The automated execution environment for a given suite. Distinct from the data it runs against. Two harnesses exist: the Phoenix (Elixir) harness and the Playwright (E2E) harness. |
 | **Characterization Test** | A test that pins the *current* behavior of an affected code path before a migration changes it — even if that behavior is defective. Written first, it goes red when the fix lands (confirming the behavior changed); a companion test asserting the *desired* behavior then goes green. Required before any schema-migration ticket that touches an untested path, per the audit finding that moduledoc-claimed behavior is often not asserted by any test. |
 | **Test Fixture** | The per-test setup data. Inserted and torn down by the test itself, not the harness. |
 | **Postgres Surface** | The minimal dependency for the Phoenix harness: a Postgres container plus a seeded `auth` schema (GoTrue-owned tables such as `auth.users`). No HTTP services. |
 | **Supabase Surface** | The full dependency for the E2E harness: Kong + GoTrue + PostgREST + Postgres. Required because E2E seeds/teardowns via the Supabase HTTP API and derives the auth cookie name from the project ref host. |
 | **Auth Schema Bootstrap** | The `auth` schema DDL the Phoenix harness relies on. The `supabase/postgres:17.6.1.136` image already ships `00000000000001-auth-schema.sql` at container init, creating the full `auth.users` table, `auth.schema_migrations`, and the `supabase_auth_admin` role. No bespoke bootstrap file is needed; the image is the bootstrap. GoTrue's own migrations run `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, so in the `supabase` profile GoTrue boots cleanly against the image-seeded table. |
 | **Shared Container** | A single testcontainer started once per `mix test` run (in `test_helper.exs`) and shared across all test cases via the Ecto SQL Sandbox. Distinct from per-test isolation (which the sandbox provides) and from per-test-case containers (rejected as too slow). |
 | **Compose-Driven Harness** | Both test harnesses drive the same stripped Supabase `docker-compose.yml` via `Testcontainers.DockerCompose` (Phoenix) and `docker compose` CLI (E2E). The compose file is the single source of truth for the stack shape; profiles gate which services each harness starts. |
 | **Per-Run Lifecycle** | The Phoenix harness does a full compose `up` at `mix test` start and `down -v` on `System.at_exit`. No cross-run reuse — every run starts from a freshly migrated DB with the Auth Schema Bootstrap applied. Deterministic at the cost of ~2-4s cold start; reuse is a deferred optimization. |
 | **Migration Deploy Shape** | Schema migrations run at deploy time via the Fly release command. Additive migrations (new indexes, nullable columns, non-conflicting CHECK constraints) deploy routinely. Destructive or non-splittable changes (column type changes, citext casts, index drops that change uniqueness semantics) use expand-contract where possible (expand → backfill → contract) and a maintenance window with write freeze for the contract step or for changes that cannot be split. Each migration ticket declares its deploy shape so the operator knows which require coordination. |
 | **E2E Deferral** | The Playwright harness E2E migration is out of scope for the current work. Only Phoenix is being reworked now. The compose file shape must support E2E later (profiles, Kong/GoTrue/PostgREST), but E2E's fixed-port and cookie-derivation concerns are deferred. |
 | **Uniform Profiles** | Every service in the stripped compose file carries a `profiles:` entry — `db` for Postgres (+ Auth Schema Bootstrap), `supabase` for GoTrue/Kong/PostgREST. No default-always services. Phoenix starts with `with_profile("db")`; E2E will later start with `with_profile("supabase")` (and `with_profile("db")` if it needs the DB too).
 | **Ephemeral DB Volume** | The Phoenix harness runs the `db` service with no persistent `PGDATA` volume — `down -v` on `System.at_exit` destroys all data. Fresh container, fresh migration, fresh `auth` schema per `mix test` run. No upstream Supabase init-SQL mounts are needed; the `supabase/postgres` image already ships `auth.users` and `pg_jsonschema`. |
 | **Root Compose File** | The stripped Supabase `docker-compose.yml` lives at the repo root next to the existing root `.env`. This lets Compose's built-in `.env` resolution interpolate `${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}` etc. without plumbing env vars through `DockerCompose.with_env/3` or duplicating the env file. testcontainers-elixir's `DockerCompose.new/1` sets `cd` to the compose file's directory, so a root-level file means `cd: repo_root` where `.env` already sits. | |

 - **Phase 1a**: Edge functions → Oban (in progress)
 - **Phase 1b**: Service layer → Phoenix API (next)
 - **Phase 2**: LiveView migration (future evaluation)

Phoenix owns authentication through generated Principals, magic links, opaque database-backed Sessions, and Assent Discord OAuth. M2 repointed application ownership and foreign keys to `principals.id`; Supabase `auth.*` remains only as rollback dead weight during observation and until the separate Postgres-hosting migration. PostgREST and RLS policies are removed when all data access is proxied through Phoenix.

+# Swoosh Is the Email Transport Seam
+
+**Status:** Accepted  
+**Date:** 2026-08-22  
+**Tags:** email, swoosh, oban, dependencies
+
+## Context
+
+Transactional emails flow through `Dhc.Email.Worker`, which today hand-rolls both halves of delivery: a `Req.post` to the Loops API in prod, and `Dhc.Email.DevMailer` — a hand-built RFC 5322 message over `gen_smtp` to Mailpit — in non-prod. Tests stub these with a `DevMailerStub` app-env swap plus Bypass HTTP stubs. A migration to Resend is planned, and apps/phoenix/AGENTS.md mandates Req as the only HTTP client while `.reach.exs` enforces it for `Dhc.*` code. The house pattern for fencing a vendor library (`Dhc.Discord.Adapter`) wraps it in a semantic behaviour.
+
+Swoosh ships first-party adapters for Loops, Resend, and Mailpit (HTTP), plus test adapters and assertions. Unlike Nostrum, Swoosh is designed to be configured rather than wrapped: provider choice is runtime config on a single mailer, not invasive API surface.
+
+## Decision
+
+Adopt Swoosh as the only transport layer for transactional email. No bespoke `Dhc.Email.Adapter` behaviour is introduced: the Oban Worker remains the domain-facing boundary (Email Kind + data variables), builds `%Swoosh.Email{}`, and calls one mailer whose adapter is chosen per environment by configuration. The Loops→Resend cutover is a config flip, not new code.
+
+Supporting choices:
+
+- `config :swoosh, :api_client, Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch` with a named `Swoosh.Finch` child — Finch is already a production dependency, keeping Hackney out of prod.
+- Non-prod delivers via `Swoosh.Adapters.Mailpit` (HTTP), deleting `DevMailer` and the `gen_smtp` dependency. Dev failure-swallowing semantics are preserved in configuration around delivery.
+- Tests use `Swoosh.Adapters.Test` / `Swoosh.TestAssertions`, replacing `DevMailerStub` and Bypass request-body assertions.
+- Sends carry `Idempotency-Key: oban-<job.id>`; deterministic provider validation failures (e.g. missing template variables) are discarded immediately rather than retried, while rate limits and network errors retry with backoff.
+- This decision documents the exception to the Req-only HTTP-client rule for the email transport seam and updates apps/phoenix/AGENTS.md accordingly. Application code continues to use Req everywhere else.
+
+## Consequences
+
+- One production dependency (`:swoosh`) is added; `gen_smtp` becomes dev-only-then-deleted.
+- Provider swaps, retries, idempotency, and error normalization move out of hand-rolled worker internals into Swoosh plus configuration.
+- The Worker's public job contract (recipient, Email Kind, data variables) does not change; queued jobs survive the refactor.
+- Reach rules need no change (Swoosh internals are outside `Dhc.*`), but the AGENTS.md HTTP-client guidance gains a documented exception.
+
+## Considered options
+
+- **Req-direct provider client** (mirroring `Dhc.Stripe.Client`). Viable — the Resend send is one JSON POST — but it would re-implement provider payload/error handling, the dev SMTP relay, and test tooling that Swoosh provides for free, and leave the team maintaining three bespoke email paths.
+- **A `Dhc.Email.Adapter` behaviour wrapping Swoosh.** Rejected as ceremony: Swoosh's adapter selection already is the seam, and a second behaviour beneath the Worker adds indirection without adding callers.

+# Code-Authored Templates Synced to Resend-Hosted Templates
+
+**Status:** Accepted  
+**Date:** 2026-08-22  
+**Tags:** email, resend, react-email, templates, ci-cd
+
+## Context
+
+Loops hosts transactional email templates in its dashboard: content and subject/sender metadata are invisible to the repository, unreviewable, and unauditable by agents. Migrating to Resend is the moment to flip template ownership. Resend offers two send models: dashboard-hosted templates (`template: {id, variables}`) or per-send inline `html`. Resend also supports authoring templates as React Email components and uploading them programmatically (official `resend` CLI; Templates API with stable aliases; draft→publish lifecycle with version history).
+
+## Decision
+
+Each Email Kind is authored as a React Email component in a new `packages/email-templates` workspace package. The component file also declares its Template metadata — default subject, default sender, declared typed variables (`string | number`, optional fallback) — making TypeScript the single schema authority for what each Kind requires. The Elixir side keeps only its generic string|number validation; Resend enforces per-template variable contracts at send time.
+
+Templates remain hosted at Resend. A sync pipeline renders components to HTML and uploads them via the official CLI/API:
+
+- Pull requests upload drafts only; merging to main publishes. Publishing therefore gates on review plus required checks, never on an arbitrary push.
+- Templates carry a stable alias derived mechanically from the Email Kind (kebab-case). Sends address `template.id` by that alias, so no kind→ID configuration map or env-var indirection exists at runtime.
+- Dashboard edits to templates are drift; the next sync overwrites them. Resend's version history is the recovery mechanism.
+
+The cutover from Loops is a single global adapter flip rehearsed against Resend's sandbox in dev (no staging environment exists), with Loops credentials kept warm for instant rollback.
+
+## Consequences
+
+- Template changes deploy through git review like all other code; agents can read and write templates.
+- The provider's template store remains part of the production path: a future provider migration must re-upload templates there. Accepted in exchange for hosted rendering, server-side variable interpolation/escaping, and zero rendering machinery in Elixir.
+- Non-prod environments keep receiving a JSON summary of Kind + data variables in Mailpit rather than rendered HTML; visual previews happen through React Email's local preview server during authoring.
+- A typo'd alias surfaces as a send-time validation error; mitigated by the compile-time Email Kind whitelist plus a check asserting every whitelisted Kind has a published template.
+
+## Considered options
+
+- **Recreate templates in Resend's dashboard.** Rejected: closest to today's shape but keeps content invisible to the repo and would be throwaway work once code ownership landed.
+- **App-shipped HTML** — render artifacts in-repo and send inline `html` per send. Rejected: makes the provider pure transport, but drags placeholder interpolation and HTML escaping into Elixir, ships rendered blobs alongside the Phoenix release, and forfeits Resend's draft/publish/versioning machinery.

**Date:** 2026-08-18

**Tags:** onboarding, discord, oauth, credentials, oban

## Context

Added and already-member outcomes both succeed. Discord 401 and 403 outcomes are terminal and do not affect membership acceptance. Success, terminal authorization failure, invalid ciphertext, and token expiry null the encrypted token. Transient Discord failures retain it only for the worker's bounded retry window.

An hourly cleanup worker nulls and deletes grants whose token expiry has passed, including grants stranded by abandoned or failed acceptance flows. No backfill is attempted for existing Members.
